Hi Aisha — attaching the items for Legal review. Summary of the key points added to the DPA addendum:

- Residency commitment: Redwood will serve production inference requests for ClearHealth from EU-hosted regions (AWS eu-west-1 or GCP europe-west1) unless a customer-approved failover is triggered.
- Transient processing window: explicitly capped at 72 hours for any automatic failover or manual emergency migration. We included clarifying language: "Transient cross-border processing may occur only to restore service and does not alter the residency commitment; persistent storage of processed customer content remains in the committed region."
- Telemetry & logs: operational telemetry required for service health (metrics, sampling) may be routed to centralized monitoring systems; any telemetry containing customer content or verbatim prompts/responses will be redacted or stored in-region per the DPA.
- Subprocessors: included current roster + per-subprocessor processing region notes. We highlighted analytics vendors and confirmed none perform permanent EU egress for customer content.

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_ClearHealth_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_ClearHealth_20260705.csv

Aisha — happy to hop on the Monday call (Irene, Ben and I plan to be on). If Legal wants a slightly tighter failover window in contract we can discuss tradeoffs (RTO/RPO impact).
